projects.title: Show HN: Formstep, Request information from customers without the back-and-forth
projects.author: mellosty
projects.summary: I built Formstep: https://formstep.io The idea came from a problem I kept running into while working on loan applications. A workflow could automate a large part of the process, but eventually it would need something only the customer could provide: a document, a correction, a signature, an explanation, or confirmation of some information. At that point, workflow automation basically did not work. The forms themselves were also often the source of the problem. Applications came in with wrong documents, misunderstood questions, incomplete answers, or people simply forgetting to finish. Someone had to email the customer, explain what was missing, wait for a reply then follow up again. It was always back-and-forth. So I built Formstep to make requesting information from customers easier, not only for humans, but also for workflows and AI agents. The idea is: A person, workflow, or AI agent sends a customer a request through email or a link. Either re-use existing form or create unique for each customer. You can prefill what you already know, lock fields, pass context, and only ask the customer what you need. For example, we might already know: * Address that you already have in the CRM * Company description from the internet * What a agreement document must contain * How a good answer should be Formstep can check inputs and uploaded files while the customer is filling out the form and tell them if something is missing or inconsistent before they submit. For example “The PDF does not contain your signature” or “Invoice total does not match the order amount”. The goal is to catch problems while the customer is still there, rather than letting bad data continue through the workflow and discovering it later. On the automation side, requests can currently be created through n8n, Zapier, the REST API, or by an AI agent over MCP. When the customer finishes, the structured answers can go back into the workflow so it can continue. Forms and invitation/reminder are multilingual, and submitted answers can be translated inside the dashboard with one click. If you want, Formstep can be used as normal form builder and shared through public links, QR, embeds etc. It support custom themes for dark/light mode, with cover image, has Notion-style editor and much more. The list is too long to fit here. I want to make Formstep a plattform where it becomes more intelligent over time and ensures that we can get better answers from customers for any use case. My question to you: Where do your automations currently stop because they need input from a customer or user, and how are you handling that today? If you are interested in trying out the n8n node: https://www.npmjs.com/package/n8n-nodes-formstep Zapier integration: https://zapier.com/apps/formstep/integrations Connecting your AI agent: https://docs.formstep.io/developers/mcp-server/ Docs: https://docs.formstep.io I would love your feedback and please try a quick demo at https://app.formstep.io/try

projects.title: Show HN: Shufler: 3D gaming harness around your coding harness and dev pipeline
projects.author: jgrichardson67
projects.summary: Hi HN. Greg here. I've been a full stack engineer for 20 years. Now all I do is shuffle messages between users, my agent fleet, our dev pipeline.. back and forth. I miss coding, solving problems, reasoning, and having an understanding and a mental model of all the work I'm juggling. But this is the job now, and there's no going back. I don't exactly feel like a 10x engineer yet, but I am for sure a 10-tab engineer. I built (er, Claude built) Shufler to lean into my new reality. If the job is basically to shuffle things through a pipeline, why not have it be more fun. Each row on the 3D gameboard is one of your existing terminal sessions. The columns are the steps your work moves through: Brainstorm, Plan, Build, QA, Review, Merge, Deploy. Your shipped PRs get stored in a warehouse/depot. The main things flowing across the board are your issues and PRs: each one rides along its session/row as it moves through review, CI and merge, and anything waiting on you turns red. I tend to manage several PRs within each Claude/Codex session, and this makes it easier for me to hold onto a mental model of where everything is. It's also made daily standups much easier to read-out. I created a few skins/themes like a casino, a theme park, sky islands, a starship and a factory, because.. of course. MacOS, works with Claude Code and Codex CLI, and cmux and iTerm (tmux should work, but I haven't tested it). It doesn't try to replace anything you already use.. just makes the orchestration more fun. You can still shift focus over to your terminal sessions when needed, use your existing skills, MCP servers, etc. There's a 3D library-building in each skin where you can specify your markdown/context folders or files, and then drag and drop to check them out by your rows/sessions. I tried to be thoughtful on security, following patterns that I consider at work. No telemetry, and the only outside calls are your own gh calls to GitHub. Daemon only listens on localhost, and every action shows its command before it runs. MCP server is opt-in, and sending to other sessions is off by default; if you turn it on, every send is a preview plus a separate confirm you approve. Details are in the README's #safety-and-privacy, and the MCP threat model (including what it doesn't protect against) is in docs/MCP.md. To report a security issue privately (or contributions to improve), see SECURITY.md. Demo with mock data, nothing to install at https://shufler.app Repo at https://github.com/jgrichardson/shufler (MIT)

projects.title: Show HN: Coding agent spots your AI practices and the ones you're missing
projects.author: milstan
projects.summary: Frontier models improve at a pace faster than the pace at which most humans are able to keep up. Not all of us are obsessed with pushing the boundaries of our agents and trying new ways to work with them. I often spend 12+ hours a day working with an LLM, and still, when I talk to people, I hear of ways of working I hadn’t thought of. What if we could speed up that pace of learning? What if everybody shared their practices of how they are making the most of AI, and if we could learn from each other? What if AI could make that sharing happen? Could everyone catch up with AI then? I know, it sounds dreamy, but my therapist says illusions are necessary—until some of them come true. I built a tool that teaches your local agent to scan your sessions, spot the best practices you already use, and guide you towards the ones you haven’t discovered yet. Only names and counts reach the server. Your sessions never do. The product has a self-consolidating catalogue of practices, MCP servers, plugins and skills. Here’s my stack—scan (locally, all session data remains private). https://app.userrank.ai/@milstan To spice things up and give a reason to rescan, I added rankings inspired by Foursquare (who here is old enough to remember Foursquare when it was gamified?). You can rank in the top 10 of a city, or of a field like Product. Claude Code, 10–20 minutes on your own plan: claude plugin marketplace add https://app.userrank.ai/plugins/marketplace.json claude plugin install userrank@userrank claude "Get my UserRank" Codex, or a quick scan of your Claude or ChatGPT chats: https://app.userrank.ai/start

projects.title: Railse：一个人同时开几个 AI 编程 agent，审批推到手机上点一下
projects.author: Railse547
projects.summary: 最近几个月我一直同时开着 Claude Code 、Codex 和 Gemini CLI 写代码。agent 本身跑得挺好，烦的是它每次要跑命令、改文件都停下来等我按「允许」。三个终端轮流翻，经常翻到的时候它已经等了十分钟；出去吃个饭，回来每个都停在第一条 git push 上。开 yolo 全放行又不敢，一句 rm -rf 出去就没有后悔药。 所以我写了 Railse：每条审批先过一遍规则，规则定不了的推到手机，我在手机上点一下，agent 接着跑。 它怎么做： - 三家 CLI 的权限钩子都接到本机一个守护进程，规则只写一套。 - 每条请求先定风险档：只读和改项目里的文件直接放行； curl 、npm install 这类联网的，git push 、deploy 这类对外的，rm -rf 、git reset --hard 这类不可逆的，都问。 - 定不了的推到手机，Web Push 通知，点开批准或拒绝。批准时勾「记住」，当场存成规则，下次同类的不问。 - 对外和不可逆的永远不能被「记住」放行，只能自己手写规则。 - Railse 自己挂了不卡 agent：守护进程没起、hub 连不上超过 30 秒，CLI 弹自己的审批框，最坏就是回到没装的样子。 hub 自己部署，一个 Go 二进制，也有 Fly.io 的现成配置；手机网页由 hub 托管，不用另外部署。命令里认得出的 token 、密码在本机就换成 再上报。 现状：v0.1.2 ，我自己在用。已知的限制：Gemini CLI 的钩子只能拒绝不能放行； Codex 的钩子只在交互会话里生效； iPhone 要加到主屏幕才能收推送； hub 是单机 SQLite 。 开源，Apache 2.0： https://github.com/xufei547/railse-opc 一行安装：curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xufei547/railse-opc/main/install.sh | sh 想听两种反馈：你同时开几个 agent 的时候是怎么处理审批的；规则表有判错的（该放行的问了、该问的放行了）直接提 issue ，我会优先看。

projects.summary: I’ve spent the last year building context for AI analysts in the mid-market. I’ve open sourced a library from my learnings, along the same principles of the Matt Pocock skills. Principles: * Claude / Codex / Cursor etc are great data agents - you just need context to enable them to answer business questions correctly. * Much of the important context lives in analysts heads' * Context must be maintainable (short, human readable - markdown and yaml) * Added context should be load bearing, not repeat of information that is available in another source of truth - and evaluations prove the value of the context * Companies should own their own context, and must be shareable with any model * Context should be version controlled (and github works as a context store). What the library does: * Performs an interview with your analysts (context-interview skill), one domain at a time, similar to what I have done as a consultant. The interview is informed by your query logs. * The AI develops evaluation questions at the same time as building the context - and at the end of each domain interview asks you to run an evaluation with and without the context. The evaluation will actually check the results against your dashboards if you allow it. We have shown increases in accuracy from 87% to 95% by adding this context in our imaginary open-source company, Shorelane. * Provides a set of skills to use the context that follow best practices for self service analytics: * Write a plain english plan for the business user to approve * Execute the plan * Verify that the execution followed the plan, and provide a simple uncertainty score. * Enable a adversarial review of the answer if their are doubts. What you get: Context repo written in markdown and yaml after you finish the interview. We use a single github repo, divided into domains. The interview can be shared and restarted by checking in/out of github. A set of skills to share with your business team Optional: We offer a fast MCP server to serve the Github-based context to your team.

projects.title: Show HN: Aigent-OS, a Claude Code harness that clears and resumes
projects.author: wrg32786
projects.summary: I run my business on four Claude Code agents: Titus, Pheme, Davinci and Metis. They write my newsletter, The AIgent (about 9k subscribers), every day through a drafting and proofreading engine that Pheme checks before scheduling. They also build AI courses, run a pipeline that turns the day's featured repo into a talking-head video of my avatar for Instagram, set up ad deals, and run Meta ads and email funnels with me. Nothing closes until I sign off. Metis posts jobs on a job board and the others claim them. The hard part wasn't any single task. It was keeping the agents coherent over weeks. Compaction kept dropping the small decisions, and then an agent would redo work I'd already ruled out. aigent-os is my fix. At a context threshold (80% by default) the agent writes a capsule, a checkpoint file in git, and has to reply with one exact line. Only then does the runner send /clear, wait for a SessionStart receipt proving a fresh session started, and resume. One ack buys at most one clear. If anything is ambiguous it stops at HOLD:clear-stalled-after-ack and doesn't retry. On resume the capsule is reference only, live state wins, and anything the writer couldn't capture is written as Unknown. First run interviews you with three plain questions and makes a first plan. Each agent gets its own memory vault. Limits, honestly: the public evidence is 11 of 11 cycles on one Windows seat. The runner can still miss a permission dialog (#104), a seat launched from inside another Claude Code session can lose its transcript (#98), and scrolling the seat window sends stray input (#99). v1.1.0 shipped on Sunday. Try bash install.sh --dry-run, it writes nothing. I'd like to hear where the loop could still double clear or strand a session.

projects.title: Show HN: Crulon – Business phone where AI does the work, humans make the calls
projects.author: rayn11
projects.summary: Hi HN, I’m Rayhan. Crulon is a business phone system where an AI agent answers the line and your team works alongside it. You can talk with our demo agent right in your browser, no sign-up: https://crulon.ai/#talk Why I built it: I’ve spent eight years as a software and network engineer, mostly building tools for internet providers, and kept watching small support teams lose customers in the seams. Calls missed after hours. Calls passed from a bot to a person who had to start over. Most voice AI products are a bot sitting on someone else’s phone line, so a handoff means forwarding to another number and losing the context. We built the phone system and the agent as one thing. What that gets you: The handoff happens inside the same system. When something isn’t the AI’s job, it asks the caller, then rings your team (in the browser or on a desk phone) with a note on why they’re calling. Live calls: anyone with permission can listen to an AI call (no one on the call can hear them) and take it over. It’s the same call, with no transfer and no hold music; the AI just leaves. Tools: the agent can call any API you define in an Action builder (look up the caller, open a ticket), and it checks with the caller before changing anything. Outbound campaigns: the agent works through a call list for reminders, renewals and follow-ups, and puts interested people through to your team. SIP desk phones, and bring-your-own-carrier so you can keep your numbers. If you run out of AI minutes, calls follow your fallback route (ring the team, voicemail) instead of dropping, and the refused call isn’t billed. How it’s built, briefly: calls come in over SIP into Call Flows (menus, queues, schedules), and your team answers in the browser or on SIP desk phones. Each agent runs on one of two engines. Classic transcribes, thinks, then speaks, so you get exact wording and English, Spanish and French. Live is a full-duplex speech model that listens while it talks and hands tool work to a second model. One fun problem with that split was teaching the agent when to hang up, which I wrote up here: https://crulon.ai/blog/teaching-a-voice-agent-to-hang-up It isn’t a CRM; it works alongside yours. Built-in Apps connect it to systems like billing and network tools, and anything with a web API plugs in through the Action builder. Pricing is per seat ($24, $49 or $89 a month) with a pool of AI minutes; human calls are included. If you sign up this month, HN30 takes 30% off the first 3 months. I’ll be here all day. Try the agent, try to trip it up, and tell me what you’d want from a phone system like this.

projects.author: donald_pinckney
projects.summary: Hey HN, I've been building Sectr, a backend-as-a-service for making it easy(ier) to develop and deploy AI agents. Deploying agents requires non-trivial systems design work. Consider a support agent: how do you stream messages to your frontend, how/where do you persist messages for frontend fetching later (or for auditing), and when the agent wants to issue a refund, do you spin-down the compute infra while it's waiting on human approval? Sectr aims to be the serverless abstraction and platform to provide these systems for you. No sign-up needed to try using the dev server: curl -fsSL https://sectr.dev/install.sh | sh # Install CLI sectr init my-agent && cd my-agent # Starter code sectr dev # Dev server, with UI to test chatting Sectr provides: - Streaming of every token, tool call and event, and persistence so they can be loaded fresh later. - Scaling up, and down to zero when the agent needs to wait, and resumption right to the suspended agent's state. - Human approved tools automatically use Sectr's suspension and resumption capabilities, no code needed from you. - AG-UI endpoint for any deployed agent so you can trivially hook up your frontend - Local dev server experience, so you can rapidly debug and iterate on your agent's behavior At the core, you can deploy any container image to Sectr as long as it implements a certain shaped HTTP endpoint. In practice, currently Sectr provides adapters to let you deploy your existing OpenAI Agents SDK, LangGraph, or Pydantic AI agents, with only 2 new lines of code: app = AgentApp(name="support") app.add_route("/chat", openai_agents(agent)) Certainly the hardest part of building Sectr was getting the resumption logic to be correct and invisible, across the Program State x Model Provider x Agent Framework matrix. For example, an earlier bug was when a model replied with text plus a tool call, Sectr would resume that as two separate messages, instead of one message with a text and tool part. This works, but breaks prompt caching (and might subtly change model behavior). Sectr is free during the beta (and can be tried locally without sign-up); I mainly want feedback, especially on dev & deployment experiences, any bugs, and what features would excite you. Introductory video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=H-y3wynkKc0 Docs: https://docs.sectr.dev

projects.title: Show HN: Limma – MCP for total recall and precision in data retrieval for agents

projects.summary: Hello, my name is Berend Graham. My cofounder Shiv Oberai and I have been working on Limma for a year now with the goal of building a proactive solution to the reliability issues that plague practical AI and agentic use in companies with RAG. Limma is a single MCP that exists for the sole purpose of ensuring that the right information is retrieved with every query and no information is skipped and or missed. This means total precision and recall. We've found that this approach leads to the lowest rate of hallucination vs. solely targeting agent action verification which has made tremendous strides in capability. We do this by building a map and structuring all data-points within unstructured data as well as federating structured data for addressability so that agents don't need to search through chunks directly and instead only get the right information . We wanted this to be extremely easy to use so that anyone can set it up and try it within minutes so that the precision issues (especially with large quantities of data) that LLMs struggle with can finally be remedied. We use self-hosted models (primarily Qwen models as of current) so that the system can be deployed on one's own server if needed, and also to optimize for speed. We have a free monthly version on our website if anyone would like to try it out and provide feedback!

projects.title: Show HN: Mainplane – Agent in Go that lives on your old PC, drives your laptop
projects.author: Alexander9
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm Alexander. Yes, this is another agent harness. Here is why I built one anyway. I was engineer #2 at Browser Use, where I built our agent harness and the evals behind it, including BU Bench, which became a default benchmark for browser agents. I left in September to build Mainplane. The problem: local agents die with your laptop, and cloud agents can't reach your work. Many cloud platforms ask you to "select a repository", but my work is not that simple. I work across a desktop, a Mac mini and a laptop, and much of it is not in git. So I loaded Ubuntu on my old 2012 desktop and made it my Mainplane server. It has run for four weeks at a load average of 0.02, because the agents' tools run on other machines. How it works: it is a control plane architecture. The server runs the harness. It holds your API keys and every session, makes the LLM calls, and routes each tool call to a worker. The workers are your other machines, connected over a built-in private WireGuard network. A bash command runs in the worker's terminal, not on the server. Shared drives let projects move across machines. The agent works on your machines just like you would, but its state lives on the server, and your keys never leave it. Some design choices: - Every session is one append-only file. This is the agent state, and it is easily readable. If something breaks, you can resume it from the file. Observability comes for free: agent traces are just these state files. - Small by design. The system prompt is 3k tokens, and there are just two kinds of tools: shell and file (read, write, edit). At Browser Use, I learned the bitter lesson and found frontier models did better when I deleted all our helper functions. So I made the same bet here: bash is all you need. - No compaction. When a session fills up, /continue starts a new one that greps the previous state file, retrieving the context it needs, instead of reading a lossy summary. A /compact on a 400k-token session takes a while to write its summary. A /continue into a brand new session starts at once. - No permission prompts. A hyperintelligent misaligned agent WILL find a way around a permission system. The better strategy is giving the agent full unbounded access to a local computer, and only putting what you trust the agent with on that computer. - Why Go. WireGuard is written in Go, so the network compiles right into a 20 MB binary. Go is made for production servers, LLMs write it well, and the simplicity of Go matches how I like to build. Mainplane works with a Claude or ChatGPT subscription on the regular usage limits, or any API key. I would love your feedback, especially brutal and honest feedback and tasks that the harness cannot do. I'll be here all day to answer questions.

projects.author: pancomplex

github.name: FrigadeHQ/hob
github.description: An easier way to use AI on your own computer. A free, open-source alternative to Claude and ChatGPT that runs open-weight models like Gemma and gpt-oss locally on Mac, Windows and Linux. Private, and works offline.

projects.summary: Hey HN, I'm Christian and this is a new OSS project I've been noodling on for the last couple of weeks. Hob is a free, MIT-licensed desktop app for Mac, Windows and Linux that works on your files the way the Claude and ChatGPT desktop apps do, except the model runs on your own computer. It uses open-weight models (currently Gemma 4 and gpt-oss). All your chats and files never leave your system. The only things that go online are web search (can be turned off in settings) and any MCP connectors you add yourself. Main features: - Automatically finds the best open-weight model for your hardware on first install (Mac/Linux/Windows) - Writes sandboxed Python code for ad hoc tools (data processing, document conversion, graphs etc.) - Built-in web search (powered by SearXNG) - MCP support - Image recognition - CRUD to your local filesystem - Works fully offline with no internet Before building this I tried every local AI app I could find, but it seemed each one had different problems. The main thing I noticed is that none of them could do what the ChatGPT and Claude apps do with your files, e.g. read and change files in a folder, look at images, run code in a sandbox, draw a chart. The most advanced thing any of them did was paste a plain text file into a small context window, which basically failed as soon as you had a file larger than a few KB. I couldn't find anything that could easily parse images and bigger PDFs. The OSS solutions that were more advanced all seemed to default to hosted models (either OSS or closed), which defeats the entire point of the privacy that on-device OSS offers. They also seemed to push towards an account/open-core style business. I build it using Electron bridged with llama.cpp in its own process. On initial load, the system will try and figure out if you have a compatible graphics card and if not default to CPU-only (I ran into a lot of issues of graphics card beeing seemingly compatible but then crashing on first query, there's a whole saga to this lol). Code execution happens in a sandbox that can only write to the chat's folder and has no network unless asked (sandbox-exec on macOS, Landlock on Linux and a low-integrity process on Windows). Images go to a small Qwen3-VL model. Dictation is a local Whisper model. The hardest part was definitely to get the smaller models to use tools reliably. Ran into a ton of issues of 4B models happily saying "here's your chart" without ever calling the chart tool or get stuck in an infinite call loop. I spent a fair amount of the work building guards vs tweaking prompts (that didn't really work for small models). I understand the pushback that local models are weaker than frontier cloud models. This is true, but for most tasks for most normal people, I'd argue you rarely need the newest frontier model. From my own evals, systems with 16+ GB of RAM do really well, and if you have a GPU or more RAM, you get very close to what you'll get out of the box with a frontier hosted model. Excited to hear what you think and see how it runs on other systems!

projects.title: Show HN: Markdown is 40× more token-efficient with SQLite
projects.author: richardcrng
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm Richard, founder of Native. I'm working on open-source context ownership, to stop AI centralisation: https://github.com/withnative/native My first focus has been making Markdown vaults powerful enough so that teams can self-host all of their context (messaging, docs and projects), without it being externally fragmented or rate-limited. I'm sharing some early results: Markdown vaults can be 40× more efficient with SQLite! https://www.withnative.ai/research-and-posts/markdown-contex... Here's some of the main ideas: - SQLite or Markdown folders, you pick. You can project the same authoritative event log into either form; more projection formats will follow (e.g. maybe neo4j; we do use a graph structure). - Empirically: SQLite is better for agents! On a 120 trial evaluation for 11,000 records, agents use 40× fewer tokens with SQLite vs Markdown, per correct answer. - Everything is a file or SQLite row. Messages, documents and projects: all can be modelled in your vault. You get local-first collaboration with teammates, synced to a cloud of your choice. - You can render your vault with arbitrary UI. Your WhatsApp-like UI speaks to your teammate's Slack-like UI; both are just views over the same database. A few things I've learned building this: - Agents do pretty well even without SQL if you give them strongly typed Markdown frontmatter. This was one arm of the trial I ran. I didn't have any clear expectations, but it was cool to watch: agents ended up writing Python scripts to do SQL-like queries. - Cumulatively, cached input tokens can get expensive. I feel silly in hindsight here. I'd gotten used to letting my sessions run long, "It's all cached so it's very cheap". But when I looked at my results here, over 2/3 of the token bill on long sessions was cached input... - "Markdown vaults don't scale as well as databases" isn't as self-evident as I think. This is why I decided to benchmark it... I've had some very blank stares when I try to explain how Markdown files might break at true agent-scale volume. Unfortunately, the dataset is private, because it's two months of my own work. I am considering open-sourcing it even so, but there is definitely some embarrassing stuff in there. TBD... I know that independent result verification matters! The core engine that I evaluated is open-source, with more to be released soon: https://github.com/withnative/native If you're interested in trying connected context on an open engine, you can get updates from our website or email me directly: richard@withnative.ai https://www.withnative.ai/

projects.title: 开源了一个 MCP 治理网关： Jev 判 0.94、d3 判 0.70，两个判官说不同的话时怎么办
projects.author: Thneonl
projects.summary: 给 AI agent 做了个 MCP 执法网关（ Rust ），核心问题：当两个决策模型对同一件事给出不同判断时，怎么安全处理？ 实测：同一个越权场景（ coding agent 试图 merge 夹带无关变更的 PR ）： - Jev 给 0.94 置信度 → 准入层 Accept → 授权挂起 → DENY - d3 （ vLLM SR ）给 0.70 → Hold → 什么都不改 → ALLOW 两个都对。分歧不是 bug ，是校准本性（ d3 ECE 4.3 vs Jev 8.0 ）。治理层的价值在于让分歧安全。 网关做的事：每个 tools/call 先过 r2r_decide 门控，ALLOW 转发上游，DENY 返回 isError + 证据文本（相位 + 规则 + 事件 ID ），全程审计到 EventStore 。 零 API key 复现： cargo run -- fixture cargo run -- fixture --provider d3 GitHub: https://github.com/Thneoly/r2r-jev （ Apache-2.0, v0.2.0 ）

projects.title: Show HN: Model Salt, fixing the pelican problem in LLMs by adding entropy
projects.author: Benjaminsen
projects.summary: I have been frustrated with how repetitive the output of LLMs is. Even at maximum temperature, asking the same prompt ten times gives functionally the same result each time, as discussed here: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50090443 That’s not surprising considering how LLMs work, but the thread above got me wondering if you could push models away from their usual generation patterns by injecting entropy from an external source. After a lot of tweaking and experimenting, I turned the idea into an MCP server. It's optimized to add just enough entropy that creative output stops being repetitive, while still living up to the intent of the original prompt. I’d love feedback, particularly on the approach itself. If you have a better way to inject entropy than what I have found, a pull request is very welcome: https://github.com/modelsalt/model-salt

projects.title: Show HN: A 3D mesh playground for coding agents (three.js + manifold-3d)
projects.author: wsxiaoys
projects.summary: When GPT-6/Gemini launched recently, a lot of the 3D demos used blender-mcp ( https://github.com/ahujasid/blender-mcp ). It's cool, but you have to install blender locally and wire up plugins just to try a prompt or share a run. I built a browser-based 3D mesh playground so you can hook up your own coding agent over MCP (or run in-browser) directly in a tab. It runs on three.js + manifold-3d for blender-like boolean/mesh editing in JS, and gives the agent a render_preview tool to take multi-view screenshots (front/right/top/iso + custom camera angles + clay mode). That way the agent can look at what it built and fix the geometry, similar to how it iterates when building a website. The submitted link is a trace of Gemini reconstructing a Copenhagen canal scene from a photo: it hits a script error on the first pass, fixes the bug, and then goes through several rounds of checking 4-view and close-up render_preview screenshots to tweak the geometry.

projects.title: Show HN: Optio – A self-hosted orchestration platform for AI agents
projects.author: jawiggins
projects.summary: Hey HN! I shared Optio here back in March. Originally it was focused on getting swarms of coding agents (claude code/codex) to drive PRs towards a merge by automatically resuming them on CI failures or PR comments. Since then, I've reworked the project to be a general platform for running any kind of AI workflow on your infra by allowing users to configure each component of a possible workflow: When: On demand, a cron schedule, or triggered by external events such as a webhook, slack message, ticket (jira/linear/gh), pagerduty/datadog/alertsmanager/pylon/sentry. Where: In a k8s pod or any machine you have installed the optio daemon on (I use my laptop). Who: Any harness you prefer (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Pi, etc.) What/Why: You can format parameters from the triggers directly into the prompts and then configure if the agent should exit, be resumed automatically, or be persistent. You can either define workflows in the web ui or as yaml files that get synced to the orchestrator (ai config-as-code). I've also built native iOS and Android apps so you can connect to your cluster and create/manage agents remotely. The marketing page is at https://optio.host and the code is still open source at https://github.com/jonwiggins/optio Would love feedback or any thoughts you might have on how I could make it better!

projects.title: Show HN: Tabverse – a free, open-source, with self-hostable server Workona clone
projects.author: liyu1981au
projects.summary: Hi, I want to share with you my chrome extension: Tabverse, as it is now passed the reveiw of Chrome Web Store and live at: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/tabverse/lffblcippn... Tabverse is a local first workona like chrome extension for managing tabs, with its source open at https://www.github.com/liyu1981/tabverse . In essential it has the core functions workona has, but can operate totally locally, which means it will not need an account nor subscription. The only limit is your local storage spaces so that you can have as many spaces(I call tabverse) as you can. It is open source, so not just your data stays with you, and the tool itself will stay with you in future. Beyond the normal workona features (persisted workspace, load/reload/import/export, note/bookmark/history tools), there are features does require a server. Features like backup/sync, global search on all tabverses, and future collaboration (not yet done), can only be possible if there is a server. I build this part in open too: the server is free to self host and open source in same repo of Tabverse. The tabverse's idea was with me few years ago while I was using Workona and was frustrated with its limitation on free tier (remember was only 5 workspaces), and the missing features of managing multiple workspaces at the same time. Tabverse takes the idea of Workona, and develop further: each window with a Tabverse tab is a workspace, all stored in local storage, and multi windows can have multi Tabverses same time, and can switch fast. There can even be window without Tabverse, so besides work, personal stuff or entertainment will have place to go. As I build this alone, in the middle, almost give up on this project, and luckily AI agents now is there: not only I have a good helper, but also I have a partner I can discuss a bit. So this time the first version starts with v0.7.2. But AI agent can never replace the real need from human on what should be built and what works better, so I want to share with you and listen to your feedbacks early. Please give it a try, and every feedback to me is a gift. Besides the self-hosted option, I host a server at https://tabverse.liyu1981.xyz (yes, the same website of intro and docs), but is invitation only. If you want to help me to test in this early stage, you can login with Google (the only social login I configured :)), and request an invitation there. I will act as soon as I find your request :). But do not worry at all if you only want to use Tabverse locally without a server -- that is the first thing when I was building it. In current version there are also AI features built in, and again do not worry as the AI features is using Chrome's Prompt API, which is totally local, with Gemini Nano (first time will need to download it automatically), nothing send to a server, and you can always turn this on of off in settings. Morden computers with decent memory should work well, but some older computer may suffer (so please turn off). And it is Chrome only. (Honestly, Tabverse currently only support Google Chrome, but not other Chrome based browsers).

projects.title: Show HN: Nodecode, open-source living agent in Lisp that rewrites itself for you
projects.author: svsairevanth
projects.summary: Hi HN, we're Mike and Thom. Agents of the future should only have one tool (the interpreter, ideally a LISP eval), nothing more or less; to interact with the world. Agents remember by writing markdown files. NODECODE remembers by rewriting itself. And that is in itself a new paradigm in working with agents. What if memories, skills, MCPs, provider connectors, tools, etc. all live under the same image as *.lisp files instead of in disarray across random folders? Ask it for something it can’t do, and it writes what it needs into its OWN running image and keeps it even after a restart. (Changes in a LISP image have significantly lower ceremony and overhead than in harnesses written in other languages): Small intuitive scenario: > you can't read PDFs. teach yourself. (defun read-pdf (path) ...) ; runs at once, kept (read-pdf "invoices/0421.pdf") ;; Globex owes $1,240.00, due Oct 24, unpaid. [… rest of PDF content] read-pdf is still there after a restart, in your terminal, and in every other UI clients (Discord, web app, etc.) Technically at a lower level; NODECODE runs as one process in SBCL, a Common Lisp system, and shells attach to it. The model has one tool: it evaluates LISP in the running program. Code is data, so a program can rewrite itself while it runs. What the model defines runs at once and is kept, one file per definition, committed with git, loaded at every start. Why LISP now? Current SOTA models have reached an optimum point in how they efficiently work with LISP, though not as fluently as Python. Still, we believe AGI will understand ANY language (past/present/future) by understanding the crux of any given language, and not through excessive and expensive pretraining scheme. Why LISP in general? We believe LISP is the current language that communicates to the world with the least bandwidth. Why another LISP agent? The LISP harnesses we found are hard to use unless you already know the language itself, and so we had this idea of simplifying and condensing the UX to be user friendly for the masses, while leveraging the power of LISP. Code as data is what lets an agent change itself, and that shouldn't need a LISP hacker to run. NODECODE is our first step toward putting it on everyone's PC and mobile. You ask in plain words, the model writes LISP, and you get briefed in natural language; that is how it should be. Extensions? Code as data also suits extensions. We see NODECODE as a living agent organism. To us, it feels very much alive, and so this brings us to the Cells system. A Cell is a folder that teaches NODECODE something new: a chat room it can live in (e.g Discord, Telegram, Slack, etc. - Yes we made Cells for channels to have it act as a very capable personal agent), a skill, a memory, MCPs, new tools, etc. Install one from our Cell hub or ask it to write a custom, personalized one. Either way it is more code the agent can read and change. Your terminal, a browser tab, your phone and bots in Discord, Telegram and Slack all attach to that SAME gateway process, so a tool it writes in one is there in ALL of them. Over time it becomes yours and it is continuously evolving; the organism within it; NODECODE. MIT License. https://github.com/nodecode-ai/nodecode X/twitter/demo launch post: https://x.com/pomterree/status/2113721985167728757 docs: https://nodecode.ai/docs

projects.title: Show HN: A Blender addon that makes Claude twice as efficient at using nodes
projects.author: carson-katri
projects.summary: I originally made this addon 4 years ago, but recently discovered that coding agents love it. The addon adds a scripting API for Blender’s node trees, such as Geometry Nodes or Shader Nodes. It generates a function and related types for every node in Blender. Then the agent (or you) can write scripts to create node trees without having to guess what the node, input, and output names are. It’s meant to be used alongside the Blender MCP. In my tests, Opus finishes building node trees in at least half the time using at least half the tokens to answer the same prompt. Because the scripting API forces it to build correct node trees, it has to back track less to fix mistakes. This saves a lot of time and tokens. There is also a skill and some helper functions to let it look up the function signatures for nodes. Let me know how it works for you!

projects.title: Show HN: Radian, an agent puts development workflow on autopilot
projects.author: anylut
projects.summary: I have built an indie hacker project; my main flow was: 1. chatting with Claud Code about the general plan 2. assigning slices of work to other worker agents like Pi + DeepSeek 4.1 Flash 3. building in parallel 4. Claud Code reviews when done, runs tests, and merges after I validate It worked, but with a lot of glue in the middle, so I built radian + arc into the same binary. Radian: a compact, pragmatic agent that has enough tooling to solve a small coding task end to end; it does not try to be a plugin platform. You can still extend it via MCP, skills, or hooks to extend its capabilities. I think plugins are great, but a lot of them are for humans. I'm trying to remove humans from the loop. Humans are at the start and end of the loop. arc: built into the radian binary; * it can get work sent from another agent * assign work items to concurrent headless radian agents * automatically review, CICD, integrate locally * humans can still be in the loop but not at the agent conversation or code review level, but at the work item approval/review level. * shows all of the above in a plan view or Kanban board in TUI. I have been heavily dogfooding, and Radian + arc basically built themselves in the last couple of weeks, with me just being a product manager/scrum master and qa. radian + arc are open source at https://github.com/hisea/radian What do you think about this approach? Looking for ideas to make Radian better or fit more scenarios.

projects.title: Show HN: pw-repl - A Playwright-powered REPL for you and your agents to share
projects.author: arcanemachiner
projects.summary: For the busy people out there, the GitHub repo has a demo video so you can see if this is worth your time: https://github.com/arcanemachine/pw-repl The video was created by Opus 5.5; I just asked it to create a demo video (it has a 'record' tool), so I think this is a good idea of how well it can work with the tool. --- pw-repl is a tool that makes it easy for you and your agents to work with Playwright+CDP in a browser (your current headed session, or a headless one, or both at the same time; take your pick). It's basically a Playwright-powered swiss army knife that helps you and agents poke around your browser: Try out different features of a website, break things (e.g. mock backend responses), take screenshots, record videos, etc. The GitHub repo shows a video, recorded by an agent using pw-repl: https://github.com/arcanemachine/pw-repl One cool thing it can do: create videos of bug reports. You can tell an agent about a bug and to use pw-repl to capture it, and it can record a video with the built-in toast feature to narrate its actions, and show a virtual mouse to simulate actions on the screen, as if it were a user. It's also useful for capturing screenshots (which can be combined with the toast and highlight tools to emphasize certain elements or information), and has many useful features that can help agents to use it efficiently. This isn't intended to be commercialized in any way. It's just a neat tool that I (with Claude's help) cobbled together. It's completely vibe-coded, and is intended mainly as a debugging aid. I use all the time, and hope it may be helpful for others. It's basically just Playwright + CDP under the hood, but has some extra tools and an interface that make it easier for agents to work with. The quickest way to try it out is to tell your agent to run `npx pw-repl@latest serve --background --launch`, which starts a headless Chromium of its own. No browser setup needed. (If you don't like such `curl | bash`-esque installation instructions, read the code, or get your agent to take a look at it.) To use it in your own browser instead, start Chrome with CDP enabled (`chrome --remote-debugging-port=9222 --user-data-dir="$HOME/.config/chrome-debug"`), and tell your agent to run `npx pw-repl@latest serve --background`. (The separate `--user-data-dir` is needed because recent versions of Chrome don't open the debugging port on your default profile.) It also can generate a skill so that you can just run `/pw-repl do some stuff`. Get your agent to run `npx pw-repl@latest skill > <skills folder>/pw-repl/SKILL.md` (e.g. `~/.claude/skills/pw-repl/SKILL.md` for Claude Code). NOTE: This has only been tested on my Linux machine, so not sure if it will work on macOS. It should, but I haven't tried it out personally. Fun fact: This tool was originally a random REPL that Claude generated on-the-fly to do some random thing. I saw it and was blown away, so I got Claude to make it into its own application. I suspect that Claude may have taken "inspiration" from an existing project with a similar name, so credit where credit is due to this other `playwright-repl` package: https://github.com/stevez/playwright-repl

projects.title: Show HN: git-dupe – Version private files alongside a public Git repo
projects.author: WayHow
projects.summary: Hi HN! I made git-dupe to solve the problem where I have notes, skills, and agent instructions that are part of my personal workflow, so I do not want them committed to the public repo, but at the same time, I want them to be in the project at the correct locations (e.g., AGENTS.md file locations matter), and these files cannot be simply gitignored because I want versioning for them. The solution that I've come upon is versioning those agent files in another repo, say <private-repo> (this repo is private to me and holds the history for my agent files). The project itself is open to the public in another <public-repo>. I overlap the two repos to solve the problem (i.e., they share the same worktree). $ git status --short # the public repo ?? AGENTS.md ?? notes/ $ git dupe init # the private repo Initialized empty Git repository in /home/brian/code/project/.git/dupe/ $ git dupe add notes/ AGENTS.md # the private repo hint: notes is now hidden from the project's Git; run from the root, 'git dupe unhide -- notes' stops hiding it $ git dupe commit -m "Notes and agent instructions" # the private repo [main (root-commit) 3eb3af9] Notes and agent instructions 3 files changed, 3 insertions(+) create mode 100644 .gitdupe create mode 100644 AGENTS.md create mode 100644 notes/todo.md $ git status --short # the public repo: nothing $ git dupe log --oneline # the private repo: your files 3eb3af9 Notes and agent instructions In short, git-dupe allows two Git repos to share the same worktree, while using native Git for most operations. Most git-dupe commands behave just like normal Git commands, operating on the private repo instead. git-dupe currently supports Linux and macOS, and is under the MIT License; the git-dupe repo contains much more extensive technical documentation documentation for those who are interested. If you have any feedback/questions about git-dupe, feel free to message. I hope it helps! Fun fact: the git-dupe project itself is using git-dupe for versioning.

projects.title: deepseek-web-retrieval：可靠的 DeepSeek Search&Fetch API 的 Coding Agent 集成
projects.author: hugo54
projects.summary: 号称 AI 原生的通用搜索引擎 [DeepSeek Search&Fetch API]( https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/search) 发布也有一周了，相信喜欢尝鲜的朋友已经为自己常用的 Coding Agent 自行 Vibe 了实现。 我也借此机会斗胆宣传一下自己对它的工程集成： https://github.com/gwokhou/deepseek-web-retrieval 希望在 DeepSeek 官方 API 支持的能力范围内，**为你提供开箱即用、更安全可靠、原生适配的工程实现。** ### 它能做什么？ - 一个安装包接通四大 Coding Agent（OpenCode / Pi / Codex / Claude Code）—— DeepSeek 官方并不提供任何宿主接入，接入层全部自研 - DeepSeek 返回的质量评分、发布时间、站点名，逐宿主验证过它们真的能进入模型上下文；你的域名黑白名单、语言偏好自动编译进查询，超长按明确优先级降级而非报错 - DeepSeek 自带“搜索即返回网页正文”，该项目补上它没有的每条长度钳制与独立超时，使正文不会撑爆任何代理的输出上限，模型按次自行开关(OpenCode 暂不支持，宿主接口限制) ### 日常好不好维护？ - 所有配置一条命令查清：实际生效值、来源、坏配置报错，可直接当 CI 检查 - 正文开销完全由宿主控制：每条正文上限、超时时长均可配置，设为 0 一键全关 - 按 DeepSeek 官方指引实现瞬态失败重试。“按成功请求计费、空结果免费”本身是 DeepSeek 的定价 ### 敢不敢让它碰配置？ - 安装前先看完整计划——改哪些文件、旧值变什么，确认后才写入；卸载完整回滚，且保留你自己的后续修改 - 路由强度按需选择，宿主做不到就明说拒绝；绝不静默降级或偷换 Provider - 密钥永不写入配置文件；内网地址在请求离开本机前就被拦下 - 返回体量有数学上限，最坏情况也不撑爆 Agent 输出（DeepSeek 未文档化正文大小，这个上限是根据各 Coding Agent 提供的一手来源算出来钉死的） ### 值不值得长期依赖？ - 完整测试、真实代理会话的端到端验证、自动化发布、逐条变更日志 - 关键决策都有带版本号的研究文档背书：锁定具体宿主版本、只引用官方一手来源

projects.summary: 先说明一下：我是 Acard 的维护者，也在负责它的内测，所以这是一条自荐。 Acard 是一个开源（AGPL-3.0）、本地优先的 Notion 式工作区。一个 Bun 进程跑起编辑器和接口，所有数据都存在你自己选定文件夹里的 SQLite 文件中，不开云功能就不会有任何东西离开你的电脑。 做它的初衷很简单：我平时大量的想法和资料其实都是在和 AI 的对话里产生的，但这些内容最后总是散落在聊天记录里。与其再手动整理进 Notion 或 Obsidian，不如让 AI 直接把对话写成页面。 主要功能： 块编辑器：标题、列表、待办、折叠块、引用、代码、表格、公式、图片，支持 / 命令和 Markdown 快捷键，可以分 2–4 栏排版。 数据库：表格、看板、画廊、列表、日历、时间线、图表 7 种视图，支持关联、汇总和公式。 内置 MCP 和 REST API：在本机运行时，Claude Code、Codex 等 MCP 客户端无需 token 就能直接读写页面，例如 claude mcp add --transport http acard 导入导出：支持 Markdown 和 Notion 导出文件。 备份：一个 zip 包含所有表、文件和每个页面的 Markdown 副本，每天自动备份。 团队使用：在局域网、家里的服务器或 VPN 上跑一个服务端，其他人用浏览器或桌面端连接。 界面支持简体中文、英文、韩文。 安装：Windows 可以直接下载 Acard Local 安装包（目前还没签名，SmartScreen 会提示，点「更多信息 → 仍要运行」即可）；macOS / Linux 需要从源码构建，或者直接 bun local/main.ts 跑服务端用浏览器打开。

projects.title: Show HN: Dánwò – Open-source E2E testing with emulators and fault injection
projects.author: faithfulojebiyi
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm Faithful. I built dánwò, an open-source (Apache-2.0) end-to-end testing framework for web and mobile apps, written in TypeScript. The problem: a UI test can click "Pay", see "Payment successful" and pass, while the card was charged twice, the webhook was handled twice, or the receipt email never went out. With coding agents writing more of our code, that gap between "the screen looks right" and "the right things happened" is where I kept finding bugs. How it works: - Tests drive the app like a user, with locators or plain-English agent steps. An agent step calls a model once; danwo records the actions and replays them on later runs with no model calls, so CI doesn't need an API key. - Your app runs behind an egress proxy. Calls to Stripe, Clerk, Resend, Slack, Google and about 20 other providers are answered by local emulators at the real hostnames, so there are no sandbox keys and no code changes. For Node apps a preload routes the calls; Bun honours HTTPS_PROXY. - An invariant is a check that runs after the test and compares two sides: what the provider says happened (charges, emails, messages) and what your app stored. For example, credits granted must equal paid checkouts times 500. - `danwo matrix` replays a test once per fault it could meet: a 500 or 429 from a provider, a declined card, a duplicate, late, forged or replayed webhook, a double-submit, a database commit whose reply is lost, Postgres unreachable for a few seconds. The invariant judges every run, so you see exactly which failure your app mishandles. - Every run leaves a flight record: video, each step, every provider call, webhook delivery and database statement, with secrets redacted. It runs in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, and on the Android emulator and iOS Simulator. It ships an MCP server and a skill, so coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) can write and run tests and fix what fails. Limitations, honestly: the emulators are only as good as their fidelity to the real APIs. Each one has a suite that runs against the real provider to catch drift, but they won't cover every edge of Stripe's API. Backend routing is built for Node and Bun today. Mobile tests need macOS or Linux. It's early (v0.1.2). The name is Yorùbá: "dán an wò" means "try it and see". Quickstart: npx @danwo/cli init (docs: https://danwo.dev/docs/quickstart ) I'd love feedback, especially on faults you've been bitten by that aren't in the matrix yet.

projects.title: [分享创造] 我做了个图片转可编辑 PPT 的工具，聊聊三类图的实际结果
projects.author: weishao666
projects.summary: 我做这个工具的原因很直接：经常收到截图或 PDF 页，要改成 PPT ，但源文件已经没了。 重画一张信息图通常要一两个小时，所以我想试试能不能把图里的文字、箭头和卡片重新做成可编辑对象。 做了一段时间，最大的感受是：这类工具的能力边界比宣传语更重要。 下面按三类图说说实际结果。 第一类，文字和简单形状为主的图，比如学术框架图、流程图、组织架构图。 这类效果最稳定：标题、标签、卡片、箭头可以分别选中，改字、改色、挪位置都不用回到原图；照片会作为独立图层保留，可以替换。 缺点是单张要 20–40 分钟，信息密集的图更久。 第二类，写实插画、照片、地图占比高的图。 这类不要期待「全部变矢量」。 照片和插画通常按区域裁切回贴，能移动、能替换，但不会重绘成矢量；如果原图里的小字本身很糊，重建出来也不会凭空变清楚。 第三类，超大图、长条图、超长截图。 这类目前不稳定：尺寸太大时，分块、对齐和渲染都容易出问题。 我的建议是先裁成关键区域，或者按页拆开处理，不要一次把整张长图丢进去。 验收方法还是三个动作：双击文字有光标、选中箭头或卡片有控制点、打开选择窗格是一组独立元素。 三个都过，才算真的能改。 我做了个开源 skill （ img2ppt ）和一个在线工具（ image2ppt.asia ）：一个给习惯 Claude Code 或 Codex 的人，一个给不想折腾环境的人。 两者能力来自同一套服务，差别在操作方式。 （环境机制图：上为原图，下为成品） ![环境机制图 · 原图]( https://image2ppt.asia/api/examples/environmental-mechanism/src) ![环境机制图 · 成品]( https://image2ppt.asia/api/examples/environmental-mechanism/out) 想请拍砖： 1. 你处理过最麻烦的一类图是什么？ 2. 20–40 分钟的等待，你能接受吗？ 3. 你更希望优先支持扫描件、长图还是手绘？

projects.title: Show HN: Corgi, a helpful {agent, terminal} multiplexer
projects.author: eiopa
projects.summary: Hey everyone, Inspired by Herdr, I've built an agent multiplexer that I've been using as my daily driver for a few weeks now. I think I improved on the concept in a few ways, focusing on the ergonomics I always wished I had: I show you what the agents are up to, along with a running feed of their activity. There's also a simple shortcut (F1) to go to the next unread agent. I use multiple accounts, so I've added unified launcher for Codex/Claude Code/Pi. Theres some careful ergonomics there: fast search and resume over sessions, inline usage tracking etc. Many small quality of life improvements to the terminal experience: - Links can be copied with a click, so no need to drag-select over many lines - cmd+v just pastes images (even on SSH) - images have a thumbnail preview. - Built-in CPU/Memory/GPU usage tracking, broken down by workspace I assume you have access to cheap inference (Luna/Haiku/etc). It just reuses the agents to organize things for you: what is this http link? what is this worktree about? what is each agent doing? It's small but it made my environment feel more cozy. On a personal note, I've been on a frustrating sick leave for a while now. I created Corgi to challenge myself, and see if I can go back. The answer is more mixed than I had hoped, but I am happy with the result and thankful for the experience. I hope you like it! a few friends & myself have been using it for a few weeks and it's been pretty nice. There's still a lot to improve and some rough edges, so feedback would be greatly appreciated. Thank you :)

projects.summary: 开源协议：MIT 我平时在好几台远程开发机上跑 Claude Code。以前的办法是每台机器开一个 SSH 窗口，再套一层 tmux，窗口一多就分不清哪个会话在等我，笔记本一合盖、网络一断，还要一个个重新连回去。 Open Walnut 是我为这件事写的自托管网页。每台主机上有一个小 daemon，Claude Code 进程归它管，所以 SSH 断了或者笔记本睡眠，远程会话都在继续跑；重新连上后，历史从磁盘上的会话日志恢复。daemon 由 Walnut 通过免密 SSH 自动部署和升级，不用手动拷文件。 所有会话在一个网页里并排看。每个会话有自己的 diff，列出它改过的每个文件（从会话日志里算，不依赖 git），可以逐行评论，再把评论发回同一个会话。旁边还有任务、笔记和长期记忆，以及一个能帮你开会话、找上下文的个人 AI。 数据都在本机 ~/.open-walnut/，没有遥测，也不需要注册账号。 安装（macOS 或 Linux，脚本自带 Node；需要一个已登录的 Claude Code）： bash curl -fsSL | sh walnut web 也可以 brew install evanzhang008/tap/open-walnut 或 npm install -g open-walnut。

projects.summary: ML Studio 是一款开源、跨平台、本地优先的桌面端机器学习工作台（基于 Electron + FastAPI + Scikit-learn + Optuna 构建）。它面向全学科科研人员（理工农医、经管金融、实证社科）与工程师，将表格数据清洗、多模型比对、贝叶斯超参数寻优、动态学术诊断看板与实验报告导出收敛进同一个极简窗口。无需繁琐的 Python 环境配置，数据不出机器，拖入表格即可自动化完成全流程。 亮点 全学科通用与零门槛：拖入 CSV / Excel 文件，自动完成列类型识别、缺失值填充与异常探测；支持回归、分类、聚类与时间序列四大建模任务。 自适应超参寻优：基于 Optuna 自动化多目标超参数搜索（TPE / CMA-ES / Random / NSGA-II），配合 Hyperband 剪枝快速提前终止无效试验。 学术级可视化诊断：实时动态渲染残差分布图、学习曲线、混淆矩阵、ROC/PR 曲线、过拟合风险预警和特征相关性热力图。 一键导出科研报告：支持一键导出排版规范的 HTML / Markdown / Word / PDF 实验报告，图表和量化结论随报告一次性生成，直接用于学术汇报。 纯本地运行，数据不出机器：所有计算与缓存均保存在本机，无第三方云端依赖，保障未发表科研成果与涉密业务数据安全。 前瞻性 AI-Native 架构 (RFC-001)：借鉴 VS Code 架构设计了 mlstudio.config.json、全局命令总线与语义控件树快照，提供本地 MCP 协议接口，支持 AI 助手免截屏、高精度直接操控软件。

projects.title: Show HN: CATT 0.2.1: Test agents/services against a Muse/Instinct-alike, in CI
projects.author: botacode

github.name: Coverage-Cat/consumer-agent-testing-tool
github.description: Consumer-agent surrogate testing for MCP servers, apps, browsers and APIs, with service-side outcome checks and sealed evidence

projects.summary: Hey HN, we recently open sourced our Consumer Agent Testing Tool to help teams iterate against proprietary assistants like Muse and Instinct. We built this to reduce our own frustrations with building an MCP/API for these agents to consume. The problem: testing against these tools is hard! Agent memory + account statefulness make reproducibility, in the ways required for repeatable/reliable outcomes, between agents and the APIs/MCPs they interact with very challenging. The solution: CATT lets devs test their services against a surrogate Muse or Instinct agent (not affiliated with either of these companies). Testers define starting conditions, approvals, and success conditions for their service's state. CATT then records the full interaction (incl. tool calls, responses) so it can diff what happened from what the agent reports. Runs can be tested in local builds or via CI, with or without LLM backing. CATT is designed to emulate the important parts of personal assistant interactions. Its got: - Tool calls and command-line tool access - Simulated approvals for service actions - Outcomes tracking and comparison - Optional MCP profile based on an unofficial Muse template There are limitations to how much we know about different assistant specific behaviors so the tool labels its assumptions as `documented`, `unofficial`, `assumed` or `unknown` for developer review. We'll do our best to keep the tool updated as new insights about the internal workings of these assistants come to light. It is an area of active research and interest, a good example is this recent report on how Instinct uses Exa for web search [0]. Are you building a connector or MCP? If yes, we'd like to hear from you! Have you had assistants behave incoherently, use stale information, or procalim success without evidence? What else should we add tests for? The best way to get started is...to point your coding assistant at the repo and ask it to integrate the tool with your CI or local testing pipeline! Hope it's helpful! [0]: https://www.sunbeam.ai/thoughts/instinct-is-using-exa-for-we...

projects.title: Show HN: Cryptex Vault – A password manager designed to outlive its creator
projects.author: Bl4cksmith
projects.summary: Hello everyone! About four years ago, a password manager I've used and depended on has been acquired and soon after, it was shut down. If anyone remembers MYKI, it was a password manager that stood out at the time. It didn't require an email address and a password for registration and it synchronized credentials peer-to-peer. It was quite handy so a couple of my friends and I got hooked, and were using it up until the last day it was online. The thing was, I didn't want to change password managers to other options available at the time, none felt right - I wanted to stay.. So I did what any sensible engineer would do 4 years ago and I wrote my own. I moved all my credentials there as soon as I had a first version ready. It was ugly (God knows I had UI/UX skills to learn), but it worked. Soon after, the same friends that were using MYKI switched over to using Cryptex Vault. I get why, we had the same P2P synchronization across devices, it was simple and didn't try to be the most-feature complete application out there - it did the job. That was an exciting moment. So exciting, in fact, that I've posted to HN to tell people about it. At the time, I had a weird thing for decentralization so I called it a "Fully Decentralized Password Manager". Three years go by, I keep maintaining the project, with no real intention of proper marketing or polishing. At one point I checked the usage and figured out that a handful of people (and their families) were still using Cryptex Vault as their password manager. Three months ago, I left my comfy job as lead software engineer at a local company to dedicate time to a company I called Cryptex Industries. Polished Cryptex Vault, cleaned it up, made it open source, started providing Docker images for self-hosting and included some of the features I've only used internally (ssh-agents). That way Cryptex Industries need not remain operational for users to have a path to continued use! To make the project commercially viable, I started offering managed services through the Online Services plan. By using Online Services you remove the operational burden of self-hosting and infrastructure maintenance from yourself while still getting the same benefits: Managed backup storage, synchronization between devices, sharing, ssh-agents, device management. It is convenience, not access to core features. The core application is free and you can use it with no subscriptions of any kind, whatsoever. It's P2P synchronized, with industry-standard crypto choices including post-quantum primitives for synchronization - https://www.cryptex-vault.com/docs/cryptography It has importers for popular password managers, along with autofill for chromium browsers (firefox is a todo, yell and I'll get on it). As for the platforms, there is a web app, an android application and an ssh-agent for linux (will put it up on AUR when they open up registrations again). Feel free to try it out (there is a 14-day trial for managed services!), self-host it or break it. I would appreciate your thoughts on this and I wish you a nice friday!

projects.author: youchibuwan-ops

github.name: youchibuwan-ops/agent-workflow-skills
github.description: Agent Skills for proactive workflow discovery, verified reuse, and reference-based editable SVG props. Codex install guides and real examples.

projects.summary: 让 Codex 主动找方法、查证据：工作流与两轮鹈鹕实测 自荐一个我维护的 MIT 开源项目：Agent Workflow Skills，目前是 Codex 预发布版，含两份可单独安装的中文工作流。 做这个项目，是希望代理遇到陌生问题时能主动找方法、核查来源、检查作品，而不总靠用户逐处指出。重点 Skill proactive-skill-discovery 把能力缺口、成熟方案检索、来源/许可证审阅、实际复用、产物验证和经验沉淀连起来；另一份 SVG Skill 则将多角度参考、结构理解、局部制作与整件复审串成流程。安装说明提供固定预发布版本的 Codex 命令及独立 ZIP。 为方便读者看实际产物，公开了两轮鹈鹕骑自行车 A/B：静态 SVG 和动画 SVG。每轮同模型 gpt-6-astra、xhigh 极高思考强度，同提示词和工具、全新隔离会话，每组上限 900 秒 / 80 次工具启动；A 不启用目标 Skill，B 只安装 SVG Skill，不显式点名调用，两轮 B 均实际读取。 静态 A 在左，B 在右： 动画 A 在左，B 在右，以下来自真实浏览器录像。B 在 900 秒预算截止前保存了可播放作品，但没有正常完成主任务。 非盲观察里，B 更明确地表达了传动、羽毛/喉囊材质和前叉制动细节，并有自主检查与纠错记录；A 也能自主修正并产出完整作品。代价同样公开：静态 A/B 约 458/568 秒，动画 A 约 519 秒，B 用满 900 秒。相同上限不等于相同 token 消耗。 这只是两轮作者案例：没有最终配对的独立盲评分，不能推导普遍质量提升；双方都没有运行中的人工纠正，不能量化“节省了多少提醒”。静态旧 B 曾被测试器误停，获授权仅补跑一次 B，旧结果和失败均保留。这两轮不是主动发现 Skill 的效果实验，后者有另行公开的干净环境流程验收记录。 中文完整案例与原件 · 主动发现的验收与限制 希望对更重视成品质量、愿意接受额外检查时间的开发者有用。欢迎复现和反馈失败，包括“检查更多但并没变好”的情况；项目不承诺每次自动触发或每次产物都正确。

projects.title: 【开源自荐】token-pilot：所有 AI 工具的本地账单 + 预算控制器（国产模型自动归一）
projects.author: anthonyhann
projects.summary: 开源协议：MIT 平台：macOS / Windows（CLI 全平台） 为什么做（背景与痛点） 我同时用 Claude Code、Codex、Kimi Code，还经常通过它们跑 DeepSeek、GLM、Kimi 等国产模型。有一天发现：我根本答不上来「我这个月给 AI 烧了多少钱」——每个工具有自己的用量页，分散、单位不一、没有总账、更没有预算。 它是什么 token-pilot = 你所有 AI 工具的本地账单 + 预算控制器。 一条命令看清今天/本月各工具、各模型烧了多少 token、多少钱；菜单栏常驻 ¥今日 · 预算%；超支系统通知；打转检测（揪出死循环烧钱的会话）；省钱建议（贵模型干轻活迁移、缓存优化空间）。 几个不一样的点 国产模型自动归一：DeepSeek/GLM/Kimi/Qwen 等靠宿主日志 model 字段识别，不用单独配置；定价表对齐 8 家官方目录价（DeepSeek 含高峰/空闲分时） 覆盖 9 个数据源：CLI 日志（Claude Code/Codex/Kimi Code/pi）、SQLite（OpenCode）、zstd 压缩日志（DeepSeek Harness）、trace（WorkBuddy）、云端 API（火山 arkcli）；读不到的工具诚实标注，不假装 数据准确性可验证：自带独立对账脚本（第三方口径重算原始日志逐项比对）+ 39 个单元测试 + 36 项看板算法不变量 零入侵：只读本地日志，不装 hook、不改配置、不过代理，数据不出本机 实测数字（作者本机，2026-10） 本月 810M+ tokens · 12,685 次调用；打转检测抓到单会话 120 次重复重试；缓存命中分析显示本月缓存省了 ¥3,048；压缩潜力量化显示上下文重发还有 $63–95/月可省。 截图 安装：npm install -g token-pilot 或 Releases 下载状态栏应用安装包。

projects.title: 【资源自荐】FusionLoop：AI Agent 时代，如何重新设计工作、岗位和激励？附 37 页论文与工作画布
projects.author: Owen-Teng

github.name: Owen-Teng/fusionloop
github.description: Organizational design & work redesign for AI agents: research paper, bilingual guides and practical canvases for roles, governance and incentives. AI 时代的组织、岗位与激励研究

projects.summary: 大家好，我是作者 Owen Teng。这次分享 FusionLoop：一套面向管理者、HR 和研究者的组织设计研究材料。 当 Agent 能完成越来越多执行工作，怎样明确谁对结果负责、谁作专业判断，以及怎样衡量协作与知识复用？这套材料尝试从一项可验收的工作出发，把人类判断、Agent 执行、组织上下文和学习反馈连起来。 读者现在可以直接获得： 37 页中文完整论文，附逐页正文与原图。 五组双语工作模板：十要素工作画布、组织权责约定、周期证据、贡献与复用、知识转化记录。 配套阅读包，含导览、主题导读与 25 项精选材料的阅读入口。 可以先选一个真实工作问题，在 工作画布 中写清结果、责任人、验收标准和证据，再讨论是否值得尝试。客户方案与人才供给是材料中的两个设计示例。 这是公开可阅读的研究与模板，不是可安装的 Agent 框架。原稿为 2026 年 8 月外部审阅校订稿，研究证据截至 2026-08-21；组织效果和跨人复用效果仍待验证，设计示例不代表实施成果。 欢迎提出具体反例：在哪类工作中，这种责任安排反而会增加协调和复核成本？问题与反馈。

projects.author: enann
projects.summary: 哈喽大家好，我是之前开发 [AppStorePrice]( https://appstoreprice.org/) 的朋友，这次给大家推荐一款订阅管理的开源方案：Calends 。 我自己一直都是订阅记录的重度用户，前前后后用过市面上十多款 App 、开源项目。但是用下来，总觉得它们跟我的实际需求，尤其是合租的场景不太匹配。YouTube 我开车快 10 年了，Spotify 也开了 5 年多。除了记录自己订了什么、花了多少钱，还要记成员付到哪天、哪些钱没收、自己到底垫了多少。再加上跨区、涨价、代付、礼品卡，很多细节都得另外补。 所以这次干脆自己做了一个，把这些年一直想要的功能都做进去。对于我自己的订阅和开车需求，我觉得目前没有比它更合适的了。尤其是现在的 AI 订阅。先放一段视频，大家可以直接看一下整体效果： [观看宣传视频]( https://media.calends.date/launch/2026-10-22/index.html) · [MP4 直链]( https://media.calends.date/launch/2026-10-22/calends-intro.16079708908f.mp4) ![Calends：AI 、合租、代付、多币种和余额续航]( https://media.calends.date/launch/2026-10-22/images/00-launch.8fe81ddc5174.png) ## 我最想说的，还是 AI 和 MCP 现在做软件，我觉得很重要的一点，就是有没有把 Agent 作为一等公民，能不能让 AI 真正帮我把事情做掉。所以在我的这个项目里，基础的 AI 创建、查询、维护订阅这些我都做了，接上自己的 DeepSeek API Key 或兼容服务就能用，收据也可以直接交给它整理，核对后添加。模型调用按你使用的平台计费。 然后是 MCP 。这可以让 Codex 、Claude Code 、Grok Bot 都可以接进来，直接管理自己的订阅账本。我现在的订阅就是交给 Grok Bot 帮我管理的。给了它邮箱权限，再接上 Calends 的 MCP ，每次有新的订阅邮件进来，就让它分析邮件，该新增的新增，该更新的更新，不用我再一条条照着填。 如果你是第一次用，直接让有邮箱权限的 AI 助手去分析历史邮件，把里面的订阅整理出来，查重、核对之后导入就行。如果你之前已经在用其他订阅管理 App ，也可以让能操作手机的 Codex 读取里面的订阅详情，再帮你导入自己的 Calends 。邮箱和手机由你接入的外部助手读取，账本这边通过 MCP 配合它完成录入。 ![Codex 、Claude Code 、Grok Bot 等 AI 助手可以通过 MCP 接入]( https://media.calends.date/launch/2026-10-22/images/02-mcp-clients.cd5cc6dca268.png) ## 还有一些功能，大家看看有没有这些痛点 **我订阅了 iCloud 土耳其区，但是它老涨价，涨价之前的价格怎么记？** 我自己这条 iCloud+，已经从 ₺64.99 涨到 ₺129.99 、₺249.99 ，再到 ₺399.99 。每次涨价的日期、之前多少钱，都能保留下来。切到原币看，也能把涨价和汇率变化分开。 ![我这条 iCloud+ 土耳其区订阅的三次调价记录]( https://media.calends.date/launch/2026-10-22/images/08-subscription-history.c40d149f78b7.png) **Spotify 开了这么多年，我到底总共付出去多少钱，收回来多少钱，亏了还是赚了？** 合租的支出、成员收款、谁付到哪天，都放在一起记。有人按月付，有人一次付半年，也能看清楚还有哪些钱没收到。 **我今天帮朋友续了 ChatGPT ，他上个月的钱付了没有？** 这种就单独记成代付，记到对应的人，收没收、收了多少都能查，也不会把替别人垫的钱算成自己的订阅消费。 **我打折买了礼品卡，面值是这么多，但实际花的钱又不一样，怎么算？** 面值和实际买入成本分开记。卡包里也可以管理支付方式、币种和余额，按后面的扣款估算还能用多久。还有一个很容易忽略的细节：我填的余额到底是哪天的余额？上周查到的数，不能一直当成今天的数，所以余额也专门做了校准日期。 包括汇率，我也专门接了。历史上每次付款，都可以按付款当天的汇率折成人民币，知道那一笔大概花了多少钱。 时间线、续费日历、各种报告图表也都做了。年付的订阅，可以分别看这个月付出去了多少钱、这个月分摊了多少费用；钱花在哪，也可以像看股票热力图那样看每个订阅占了多少。这些看起来都是小功能，但自己长期记订阅、开合租车的时候，确实都会用到，所以我把它们都补上了。 ## 部署和体验 可以直接用 Docker ，放到自己的服务器、NAS 上；也可以用 Cloudflare 账号部署到 Workers + D1 ，个人用量在免费额度内就能免费运行。支持备份恢复和 CSV 导入导出。 - 官网： https://calends.date - 文档： https://docs.calends.date - Demo： https://demo.calends.date - GitHub： https://github.com/imetn/calends 最后，我还专门做了一个彩蛋。**Claude 封号这个事情，我到底被封了几个号？有没有退款？没退的话，到底损失了多少钱？** 这些也可以记。我专门做了一个 [Claude 演示站]( https://demo.calends.date/claude/)，把账号停止、退款、没用完的时长和损失都放进去，大家可以直接进去看。演示站用的是虚构数据，主要给大家演示一下这种被封号的账怎么记。 其实我直接建议，这些事情全都交给 AI 就好了，让他帮我记录好我自己的订阅账，而且我测试下来，自己反代出来的 Deepseek 模型已经完全足够了，本身多模态也支持。粘贴上传图片记录订阅也是一个非常棒的体验。 一不小心说了这么多，总之吧，我觉得大家感兴趣可以去演示站试用一下看看，不关你是上百辆合租的车主，还是中转站几百个 Claude 账号的老板，都可以看看当前的方案能不能满足你的需求好好 项目是 MIT 开源的。如果有些场景还满足不了你的需求，欢迎直接提 [Issue]( https://github.com/imetn/calends/issues)，也欢迎 PR 。如果你自己想做深度定制，直接 fork ，搭自己的订阅账本就好。 如果你觉得这个项目有帮助，不妨在 GitHub 帮我点一个 Star ，这对我来说会非常有帮助。谢谢大家！

projects.title: 【工具自荐】remote-assist-tool：一个协助码，让 AI 助手直接调试远端机器
projects.author: kegechen

github.name: kegechen/remote-assist-tool
github.description: Remote assistance with a one-time code: let your AI agent (Claude Code, Codex…) debug a remote machine via MCP, or open an SSH tunnel. Relay / LAN / P2P, no public IP needed.

projects.summary: 我是 remote-assist-tool 的作者，提交给周刊编辑筛选。 remote-assist-tool 是一个命令行远程协助工具，Go 编写，单个二进制，MIT 协议开源。被协助的一方运行 remote share，拿到一个协助码；协助方用这个码就能连上去，不需要公网 IP，也不需要在对方机器上配置 SSH 服务端或开端口。 它有两种用法： 1. 传统 SSH 远程协助：协助方运行 remote help --code <协助码> --legacy-ssh，本地就有一条到对方 SSH 的隧道。 2. 让 AI 助手直接操作远端机器：remote help --mcp-stdio 本身就是一个标准的 MCP server，Claude Code、Codex、豆包等支持 MCP 的 AI 工具都能接入。配置好以后，对 AI 说一句"协助码 xxxx，连上去"，它就能在远端执行命令、读写文件、看进程、查日志、上传下载文件（一共 12 个工具），用来远程排查问题。被协助端的终端会实时显示 AI 执行的每一个操作。 bash 安装（Linux / macOS / Windows Git Bash，amd64 和 arm64 都支持） curl -fsSL | sh 被协助端：生成协助码，默认 30 分钟后过期 remote share 协助端：用协助码建立 SSH 隧道 remote help --code ABCD-EFGHIJ --legacy-ssh 其他特点： 三种连接方式：经公网中转服务器转发；同一局域网内用 --standalone 直连，不依赖任何外部服务器；NAT 打洞 P2P 直连，打洞失败会自动回落到中转。 中转服务器可以自己部署（Windows / Linux / macOS 都有预编译版本，Windows 还能装成系统服务）。也有一个内置的公共中转服务器，开箱即用，但它在海外，而且中转服务器属于信任边界，所以敏感环境建议自己部署。 链路使用 TLS 加密，AI 工具通道再用协助码派生的密钥额外加密一层；支持命令黑名单/白名单。

projects.title: Show HN: Loudwalk – Review your Anki deck out loud on a walk
projects.author: cracadumi
projects.summary: Hey HN, Loudwalk ( https://loudwalk.com/?from=hn ) is an app I built for myself to review my Anki flashcards out loud on a walk, and am excited to share today. Anki has changed my life and is probably the best habit I've managed to stick with. Apart from helping at my tech day-job and remembering random things I find interesting (relatives' birthdays, quotes, poetry), it allowed me to become conversational in Russian in 2 years and complete the first year of a French university degree in Art History - all while working full-time as CTO and co-founder at my company. I have an average memory at best, and it is crazy what Anki unlocks with consistency. Recently I've been exploring how interacting with LLMs by voice can help me spend less time at a screen and more time active and outdoors, for two main reasons: - wanting to be more active/healthy as I'm in my mid-thirties and starting to get back pain - just had a newborn and spend a lot of time carrying him or doing chores around the house Most of my time sitting at my desk is spent waiting for coding agents and reviewing Anki cards. After building Notiferry ( https://notiferry.com/ ) to forward macOS notifications to my iPhone, the next obvious move was Loudwalk: an LLM asks your card questions, listens to your spoken answer, and grades it. Voice reviews give a cadence I don't have on screen, cutting my daily review time in half (from 90 minutes to 45), and walking while reviewing helps both memorization and mood. Time simply doesn't have the same flavor staring at a monitor vs walking in nature or holding your baby. What Loudwalk does: - Import your decks with full history and media from Anki (and export back to Anki with no lock-in; includes a starter deck and CSV import if you don't use Anki yet) - Start a voice review from any deck (works with Siri so your phone stays in your pocket) - Spoken grading + "deep dives": if you stumble on a card or want context, ask out loud to start a live conversation on the subject, with live web fact-checking when dates or connections matter. Say "next" to return to your queue - Question rewording: rephrases questions so you memorize the concept, not the exact card wording - Phonetic grading + deterministic timing: on-device STT mangles proper nouns, so the LLM grades phonetically/semantically against your card's answer, while response-time caps (Again/Hard/Good/Easy) are applied deterministically in code - On-device speech recognition; grading and deep dives use OpenAI models (a mix of GPT-6 Luna and Sol + GPT-Live-1) It runs on iPhone (iOS 26) and Apple silicon Mac (macOS 26). No Android or Windows. I haven't planned to open-source it for now as I'm seeing if it can support me working on it long-term. Visual reviews (Anki-style) are free forever; voice reviews require a subscription ($9.99/mo) after a 7-day trial (no account or credit card required). Sync across Mac and iPhone uses append-only JSONL review logs in your own iCloud Drive - no server in the sync path, and visual reviews + sync + export work offline forever. I switched to Loudwalk over 3 months ago (>3k spoken reviews) with first-class support for English and French, plus a CLI so coding agents can add cards at the end of a study session. Happy to answer any questions about the app or spaced repetition!

projects.title: Show HN: Mnemolith – AI coding memory that goes stale when your code changes
projects.author: Anish2910
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm Anish. I built Mnemolith because the AI coding tools I use (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) either forget my project between sessions, or remember things that quietly stopped being true. Tell the agent "we use Postgres", migrate to MySQL two weeks later, and it keeps building on the old fact. How it works: - It's an MCP server, so Claude Code, Cursor and Codex share one memory per project (keyed by the git repo). - When the agent saves a memory, it can link it to the files it depends on. Mnemolith stores each file's git blob hash. If the file's contents change (committed or not), the memory is set aside and flagged for review, so the agent stops relying on it. - A local dashboard shows what the agent remembers, where each memory came from (tool, session, file versions), and its full history. You can confirm a memory is still true, or retire it and say what's true now. - Contradictions are judged by the agent, not by a similarity threshold. In my calibration, "we use Postgres" vs "we migrated to MySQL" only scored 0.30 similarity, so a threshold can't tell a contradiction from an unrelated fact. - Current memories can sync into a managed section of AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md, so they get reviewed in PRs. Under the hood it runs on an engine I wrote from scratch in Java: a Redis-compatible server with a built-in memory model and an HNSW vector index. Embeddings run locally (all-MiniLM-L6-v2). Everything stays on your machine. It's early (v0.2.1). There's no team sync yet beyond the AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md files, and it needs Java 11+ (it downloads a private copy if you don't have one). I'd really like feedback, especially from people running coding agents on real codebases. What does your agent keep getting wrong?

github.description: Local-first AI second brain & personal knowledge management: Six-Brain Markdown blueprint, Obsidian example vault, offline deployment and bilingual guides. 六脑方法 · 本地知识管理

projects.summary: 大家好，我是 Owen Teng，FridayOS 的参与者。这次想自荐一个开源的个人知识管理实践：FridayOS 1.0。 这个项目想解决的问题是：原始资料、正在推进的任务、已经形成的认识和可复用的方法容易混在一起。项目用“六脑方法”把它们分工，再通过来源与反馈联系起来： | 区域 | 负责什么 | |---|---| | inbox | 接住新材料与想法 | | exec | 记录目标、进展和下一步 | | wiki | 积累有来源、可复用的知识 | | skills | 保存经过检验的重复做法 | | raw | 保留原始依据 | | system | 写清规则与 AI 的操作边界 | 这次公开的材料包括： 完整离线蓝图部署包：生成 Markdown 目录、规则与空白模板，支持预览、创建和检查。 可在 Obsidian 打开的中文虚构公司示例，附 11 个练习提示词。 中英文方法与部署教程，代码采用 MIT 许可。 中文介绍 · 部署步骤和下载入口 蓝图部署只需 Python 3.9+，下载后可离线运行；AI 模型和插件需要另行配置。当前部署验收基于 Windows，其他系统、AI 接入和真实使用成效仍需单独验证。“六脑”是组织知识的设计类比，不是脑科学效果主张。 希望它能帮助正在尝试本地知识库或 AI 第二大脑的读者。也欢迎反馈：从下载到第一次整理材料，哪一步最难理解？

projects.title: Rings
projects.summary: Rings cuts any Git repo open like a tree trunk: one ring per month since the first commit, wider when the month was busier, coloured wherever the commit history itself discloses AI: a Co-authored-by or Assisted-by line naming a coding agent (Claude, Codex, Copilot, Cursor…), an AI agent's own account, or a bot-named account. Browse 37 famous repos or ring your own with an open-source Agent Skill and CLI. Node built-ins only, no API keys, nothing uploaded. Disclosure is not usage.

projects.title: Agentic Commerce Readiness
projects.summary: Enter your website for a free readiness report.An experiment from a payments practitioner. Enter any store URL and get a free agent readiness report: can AI shopping agents find, check out and pay on your site, and who carries the risk when an agent order goes wrong. It checks public signals like llms.txt, robots rules,well-known files, UCP and MCP endpoints, plus policies. It also runs as an MCP tool,, so your own agent can call it. Early and imperfect, so feedback is very welcome.

projects.title: Figma code layers
projects.summary: Figma’s code layers put working code on the design canvas, next to the designs. Create one from a frame, a GitHub repo, a webpage via Chrome extension, or by asking the Figma agent. Compare options side by side, and turn a code layer’s states back into editable layers. Figma Specs add design and technical requirements on the canvas, and Payload connects data to Make. Public beta.

projects.title: [开源自荐] GFT Map：在 AI 新会话开始前，检查要带走的决定与理由
projects.author: CoralLips

github.name: CoralLips/gft-map
github.description: 可看、可改、可带走的 Agent 主题上下文。Local, editable context maps for AI agents.

projects.summary: 我是 GFT Map 的维护者。它是配合 Codex、Claude Code 使用的本地应用，附有供这两款工具调用的操作说明（Skill）：把一个主题的对话材料整理成可编辑文稿，并用图连接决定、理由和待解决问题。人先检查、纠正，再让新会话读取该主题，接着工作。 不用安装的中文预设例：点“银行自动同步暂缓？”看取舍理由，切到文稿，再预览要交给下一场聊天的文本。演示内容是虚构的，不调用模型。 另附作者已审阅的真实交接稿：游戏作者希望玩家在聊天里下令，同时留在原地图。作者审阅后补充，如果必须打开控制面板，应先征得玩家同意。这项条件已补进交接稿；读者可以直接读文稿，无需安装。完整原讨论。 开源仓库与安装，MIT 协议。需要 Node.js 22.20+ 和已登录的 Codex 或 Claude Code，AI 整理消耗对应账户的模型额度。 当前限制：手改文稿和节点说明不会自动互改，需要核对一致；真实案例完成的是文稿审阅，新会话接续及 Map 相对普通 Markdown 的收益尚未验证。本文及案例说明由维护者借助 AI 整理。

projects.title: Peras
projects.summary: Peras puts a line in your Claude Code and Codex week. Set it (peras set weekly 85 pause) and once usage crosses it, the agent's next tool call is refused with a plain reason, so one long task can't burn the rest of your week. Resume whenever you want, from the terminal or the menu bar. Opt-in: your agents can be told their own usage. The CLI and hooks are free and MIT. The native Mac menu bar app is €4.99 once.

projects.title: 【产品设计自荐】Companest 伴境：把 AI 工作伙伴放进一个有房间和角色的小世界，从邮件事项开始

projects.summary: 大家好，我是 Owen Teng，与 Robinson AI Lab 共建 Companest，负责产品方向、交互设计、前端探索和产品呈现。想分享一个工作场景 AI 产品的交互探索：Companest · 伴境。 它尝试让“找到要处理的事、看清上下文、决定下一步”更直观：房间组织工作入口，角色提供亲近感，事项板集中呈现需要关注的工作。邮件是第一个可用的预览工作流。 目前可以公开查看： 六位助理的场景动画，以及每项能力的当前状态。 邮件事项、上下文、可编辑回复与后续变化的 五步实机截图分镜和功能说明。 产品创意由来 和 获取及数据边界。 当前是 Windows 邮件预览 0.3.26 的产品展示，源码和安装包尚未公开。163 邮箱与可选 AI 建议需要用户自己的受支持环境。其余五位助理的动画已经存在，不代表完整业务工作流已接通；截图使用独立虚构数据，分镜不是连续录屏，也没有据此宣称效率提升。 欢迎从交互角度给建议：看完演示后，你能否判断哪个事项需要你处理，以及一封新回复会怎样改变原来的草稿？可以在 反馈区 描述一个不含私人信息的具体场景。

projects.title: mcpspan

It also shows what your tool list costs agents in tokens, and which tools they never use. Open source (MIT), with SDKs in eight languages: TypeScript, Python, Go,NET, Java, Rust, Ruby and PHP. Self-host it free with every feature, or let mcpspan Cloud run it.

projects.title: Betterdata

projects.title: Show HN: Sonah, code reviewer that reads your agent's session, not only the diff
projects.author: abhinavsoni
projects.summary: Hey Everyone, After getting frustrated by Claude rewriting key functions and still making the test pass, was tinkering around with a review tool, that would track the assumptions and decisions the agent took, without me digging through the entire session. So ended up building Sonah. Sonah is basically a code reviewer that not only reads the code and diff but also the agent session that wrote the code, to understand the assumptions, and decisions your agent took along the way. And highlight important parts of the code that need your attention. Sonah uses your existing claude code/codex subscription (claude preferred for higher context window). You can try using below: npm install -g getsonah sonah doctor cd your-project && sonah review --format html --output ~/review.html

projects.title: Show HN: Buildnotes – Turn pull requests into "how it's made" posts
projects.author: zachdunn
projects.summary: I've been working on a way to take existing pull requests and turn them into "How It's Made" style content you can use outside of Github. buildnotes is an agent skill that reads a feature's issues, PRs, commits and reviews, then produces a post with real figures. Those include flow diagrams, annotated screenshots with notes in the margin, before/after comparisons, charts and real code. Also supports videos + slides, so you can share them externally too. Open source: https://github.com/buildinternet/buildnotes

projects.title: KanbanMCP

Agents claim cards, check in while they work and leave a handoff note, so the next agent starts where the last one stopped. You see every move with the name of the agent that made it, answer their questions, and cut any agent off in one click. Free to start.
